name: Blockchain & Smart Contract Security
description: Security of blockchains, consensus, cryptocurrencies, DeFi, and smart contracts.
narrative:
USENIX Security's earliest work in this area (2018) wrestled with the foundational tension of programmable money: how to make smart contracts both scalable and secure. "Arbitrum: Scalable, private smart contracts" (2018) attacked the performance and privacy limits of on-chain execution, while "teEther: Gnawing at Ethereum to Automatically Exploit Smart Contracts" (2018) showed that contracts holding real money were riddled with automatically exploitable bugs. Alongside these, "An Empirical Analysis of Anonymity in Zcash" (2018) probed whether the privacy promises of cryptocurrencies actually held up in practice, setting an empirical, measurement-driven tone for the field.

The next phase shifted from "can we break individual contracts" to "how do attackers actually behave in the wild." "The Art of The Scam: Demystifying Honeypots in Ethereum Smart Contracts" (2019) catalogued contracts deliberately designed to trap greedy users, and "StrongChain: Transparent and Collaborative Proof-of-Work Consensus" (2019) pushed on the consensus layer itself. By 2020, analysis tooling matured into rigorous program-analysis territory with "ETHBMC: A Bounded Model Checker for Smart Contracts" (2020) and "TXSPECTOR: Uncovering Attacks in Ethereum from Transactions" (2020), which reconstructed attacks directly from on-chain transaction traces. "An Ever-evolving Game: Evaluation of Real-world Attacks and Defenses in Ethereum Ecosystem" (2020) framed security as a continuous arms race rather than a one-time audit.

The early 2020s brought a decisive turn toward economic and ecosystem-level threats. "Frontrunner Jones and the Raiders of the Dark Forest" (2021) gave the first large empirical account of frontrunning and what would become known as MEV, while "Smart Contract Vulnerabilities: Vulnerable Does Not Imply Exploited" (2021) tempered earlier alarmism by showing that many flagged bugs were never actually attacked. Tooling kept advancing with language-model-guided symbolic execution in "SmarTest" (2021), and the lens widened beyond Ethereum to other platforms in "EOSAFE: Security Analysis of EOSIO Smart Contracts" (2021) and to whole decentralized applications in "Evil Under the Sun" (2021).

Most recently the field has matured into studying the complex financial machinery and upgrade patterns of live DeFi. "A Large Scale Study of the Ethereum Arbitrage Ecosystem" (2023) measured the real economy of bots and arbitrage that now defines on-chain finance, and "Proxy Hunting: Understanding and Characterizing Proxy-based Upgradeable Smart Contracts in Blockchains" (2023) confronted the security implications of contracts that can be changed after deployment. The trajectory runs from breaking single contracts, through automated and model-checking tooling, to empirical, economy-aware analysis of how value and attacks flow across the entire blockchain ecosystem.

milestones.title: teEther: Gnawing at Ethereum to Automatically Exploit Smart Contracts
milestones.note: first to automatically generate working exploits against money-holding Ethereum contracts, launching the smart-contract security agenda

milestones.title: An Empirical Analysis of Anonymity in Zcash
milestones.note: set the empirical, measurement-driven approach to evaluating real cryptocurrency privacy guarantees

milestones.title: The Art of The Scam: Demystifying Honeypots in Ethereum Smart Contracts
milestones.note: shifted focus from contract bugs to adversaries actively deceiving users, mapping in-the-wild scam behavior

milestones.title: ETHBMC: A Bounded Model Checker for Smart Contracts
milestones.note: brought rigorous bounded model checking to smart contract analysis, advancing the tooling state of the art

milestones.title: TXSPECTOR: Uncovering Attacks in Ethereum from Transactions
milestones.note: reconstructed real attacks directly from on-chain transaction traces, pivoting analysis toward live blockchain data

milestones.title: Frontrunner Jones and the Raiders of the Dark Forest: An Empirical Study of Frontrunning on the Ethereum Blockchain
milestones.note: first large empirical study of frontrunning, opening the economic/MEV dimension of blockchain security

milestones.title: Smart Contract Vulnerabilities: Vulnerable Does Not Imply Exploited
milestones.note: reframed the field by showing many reported vulnerabilities are never actually exploited, grounding risk in reality

milestones.title: Proxy Hunting: Understanding and Characterizing Proxy-based Upgradeable Smart Contracts in Blockchains
milestones.note: tackled the security of upgradeable contracts, marking the field's move to mutable, production-scale DeFi systems
